evidence: placeOrder delegates to Order.place, product.ensureAvailable and product.reserve. It only coordinates them and saves through this.orders and this.products.
transition calls order.advanceTo, so the state-machine rule lives in the domain. The service only triggers product.dispatch when the target is "shipped".
cancel calls order.cancel, then product.release for each line. This is cross-aggregate orchestration, which belongs in the application layer.
Dependencies are injected as domain port interfaces (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, IdGenerator, Clock). The file has no HTTP, storage or framework code.

It loads aggregates through repository ports, delegates business behaviour to domain objects (Order.place, order.advanceTo, order.cancel, product.ensureAvailable, product.reserve, product.dispatch, product.release), coordinates across aggregates (stock reservation, release and dispatch on state changes), and persists through injected interfaces. It has no persistence, transport or framework logic. The only rule-like code is the empty-items check in placeOrder. That is command-level input validation, which fits the application layer. The state-machine rules, stock availability and lifecycle transitions stay in the domain.
